stem: A nurse is caring for a hospitalized client who has undergone an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) and requires a Protective Environment. Which room characteristic is appropriate?

options.A: HEPA-filtered incoming air with positive pressure relative to the corridor and at least 12 air changes per hour.
options.B: Negative pressure relative to the corridor so air from the hallway is continuously drawn into the client's room.
options.C: An ordinary private room without special ventilation because Protective Environment controls are not used for allogeneic HSCT recipients.
options.D: A room that relies primarily on routine gowns and gloves for every entrant instead of environmental air-control measures.

rationale: CDC recommends a Protective Environment for allogeneic HSCT recipients to reduce exposure to environmental fungi. Core environmental controls include HEPA filtration of incoming air, positive room pressure relative to the corridor, a well-sealed room, directed airflow, and at least 12 air changes per hour. Negative pressure is used for airborne infection isolation rather than routine Protective Environment function. CDC also states that a Protective Environment does not require barrier precautions beyond Standard or Transmission-Based Precautions and does not support automatically placing every other immunocompromised population in a Protective Environment.
educational_objective: Differentiate the specialized Protective Environment used for allogeneic HSCT recipients from routine infection precautions and identify its key ventilation features.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Guideline for Isolation Precautions — Precautions to Prevent Transmission of Infectious Agents; Appendix A Table 5: Components of a Protective Environment; Summary of Recommendations
source_version_date: CDC pages updated 2023-11-22 to 2023-11-27; recommendations edited July 2023 without change in intent
source_locator: Section III.F, Protective Environment; Appendix A Table 5, Patients: allogeneic HSCT only; Summary of Recommendations, VI.A-VI.C.1
source_claim_supported: CDC recommends Protective Environment placement for allogeneic HSCT patients and specifies HEPA-filtered incoming air, positive pressure relative to the corridor, well-sealed rooms, directed airflow, and at least 12 air changes per hour. Routine extra barrier precautions are not required in the absence of another indication.

correction_summary: Completely rebuilt the original generic 'immunocompromised precautions' item because its claims were too broad and duplicated prior neutropenia/visitor-screening items. The final construct is the CDC-defined Protective Environment for allogeneic HSCT recipients, with exact environmental specifications and an explicit distinction from negative-pressure isolation and universal use in all immunocompromised clients.
audit_findings: Original item treated heterogeneous immunocompromised populations as if one universal precaution bundle applied equally in hospital and home settings.
CDC specifically defines Protective Environment use for allogeneic HSCT recipients and gives objective ventilation requirements.
The final item avoids suggesting routine negative-pressure isolation, unnecessary universal barrier precautions, or PE placement for every immunocompromised patient.
The construct is distinct from Q1743 neutropenia discharge teaching and Q1748 symptomatic-visitor source control.
Independent adversarial review found one uniquely correct response with no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, or unresolved source conflict.
